title: Parthian Mesopotamia
subtitle: 141 BC – 224 AD · The Land Between the Empires — Ctesiphon the Arsacid Capital, the Wars with Rome, the End of Cuneiform, and the First Rabbis and the First Churches

categories.label: Power
categories.subtitle: Mithridates I's conquest and the Arsacid settlement, Mithridates II at the height, the long stand-off with Rome from Carrhae to the Severan sacks, the client kingdoms of Characene, Hatra and Edessa, and the fall to Ardashir

categories.label: Conflict
categories.subtitle: The destruction of Crassus at Carrhae, the Parthian thrust into Syria, the seven-year revolt of Seleucia, Trajan's sack of Ctesiphon and the Jewish war in the rear, the burning of Seleucia in 165, and the Sasanian revolt

categories.label: Order
categories.subtitle: The King of Kings and the loose confederation of the great houses, the twin cities of Ctesiphon and Seleucia, the Greek self-government of Seleucia preserved, the temple assemblies still meeting, and the shift from clay to parchment

categories.label: Belief
categories.subtitle: The last cuneiform tablet and the end of the three-thousand-year tradition, the exilarch and the first Babylonian rabbis, the first churches at Edessa and Ctesiphon, the old gods of Babylon and Hatra, and the baptising sects of the lower canals

categories.label: Expression
categories.subtitle: The final colophons in cuneiform, the rise of Syriac as a literary language, Parthian frontal art and the sculpture of Hatra, the rebuilt showcase cities, and the Chaldean astrology handbooks in Greek

categories.label: Thought
categories.subtitle: The last Babylonian astronomers and their almanacs, Ptolemy building the Almagest on their observations, astrology as a Roman science, the world of the Babylonian Talmud taking shape, and the incantation-bowl tradition

categories.label: Economy
categories.subtitle: Ctesiphon and Seleucia as the great emporium of the East, Parthia the middleman of the Silk Road, Characene and the Palmyrene Gulf trade, the agrarian base still rich, and the Arsacid silver drachm

categories.label: Technology
categories.subtitle: The palaces of Ctesiphon and the birth of the iwan, the vaulted open hall that would define the region's building for a millennium, Parthian brick vaulting and the ashlar of Hatra, and the shifting river channels

categories.label: Exchange
categories.subtitle: Mesopotamia the permanent frontier war-zone between Rome and Parthia, the Palmyrene caravan colonies, the embassies to and from Han China, the Jewish network linking Babylonia and Palestine, and the Christian mission moving east

categories.label: World
categories.subtitle: The land between the empires, the Aramaic renaissance as Greek recedes and cuneiform ends, the three faiths taking root in the same cities, and the loose Parthian overlordship the Sasanians would inherit and centralise

categories.label: Lives
categories.subtitle: The last scribe of the Esagila, the exilarch at the Arsacid court, the Palmyrene caravan merchant at Charax, the Syriac-speaking Christian of Edessa, and the Parthian nobleman of the great houses
